newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli MP rebuked for slur against U.S. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Israeli MP rebuked for slur against U.S. envoy.

text.p: The Israel government's Forum to Combat Anti-Semitism has rebuked a Jewish lawmaker for slurring U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk.

"Use of anti-Semitic terms here in Israel, and especially by a public official, is injurious," Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, who chairs the forum, said in a letter to Rehavam Zeevi, leader of the ultra-nationalist Moledet party.
"It is especially saddening that the use of the terms attributed to you were directed at Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk," the letter released by Naveh's office on Thursday said.
Participants at a meeting this week in parliament to push Jewish settlement quoted Zeevi as calling Indyk a "yehudon" -- a Hebrew slur variously translated as "Jew boy" or "Yid".

"I told him to take it back both out of respect for America and the Jewish people," legislator Ruby Rivlin of the ruling Likud, who was present at the meeting, told Reuters. "Since it was a side meeting, there was no way to call him to order".
A U.S. embassy spokesman said Indyk was offended.
"He felt profoundly offended, as any Jew would, that such an anti-Semitic expression would be used," spokesman Richard Scorza told Reuters.
Zeevi was not immediately available to comment.
